stories.headline: Man United head coach Michael Carrick arrives at Carrington amid doubts over his future
stories.summary: Under-fire head coach Michael Carrick has arrived at Carrington after Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held talks over his future.
stories.body:
Under-fire head coach Michael Carrick has arrived at Carrington after Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox held talks over his future.

The popular former Red Devils midfielder not only steadied the ship after Ruben Amorim's rocky reign but helped it change course as his January arrival inspired the side's rise to third in the Premier League.

Carrick's impressive stint saw him rewarded with a two-year deal to stay on as United boss, but just five months later he is facing the sack following Sunday's 3-0 Old Trafford loss to Bournemouth.

Talks over the managerial situation followed that defeat and continued after Berrada and Wilcox arrived at the Carrington training complex on Monday morning, the Press Association understands.

Carrick arrived at the training ground shortly before 2 p.m. as United Under-21s took on Hull -- the side that helped ensure United got their Premier League season off to a nightmare start -- in a behind closed doors friendly.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are potential replacements for Carrick, sources told ESPN.

Carrick's side are without a win in eight games after being beaten by Bournemouth days after the 4-1 Champions League loss at Como.

United have won just two of their 12 matches in all competitions this term and their seven-point return from eight matches represents their worst start to a season since 1986.

The side sit just a point above the Premier League relegation zone in 16th place ahead of Saturday's trip to Chelsea, before heading into the international break with home games against Roma and Aston Villa.

Carrick sidestepped questions over his future following the Bournemouth defeat but appeared to know the writing was on the wall as he waved to the crowd and patted his chest as he exited the pitch, with fans supportively chanting his name.

The Old Trafford faithful's anger was instead aimed at the Glazers, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Ineos set-up, including United director of football Wilcox.

Players were booed at the final whistle and then fiercely as they followed Carrick down the tunnel on a day when the manager left skipper Bruno Fernandes on the bench.

- Sources: United consider Howe, Nagelsmann to replace under-fire Carrick

- Man United are in crisis (again), but where are the Glazers?

- Man United are stuck with their underperforming players no matter who's manager

The 32-year-old has been a pale imitation of the player who won last season's Professional Footballers' Association and Football Writers' Association awards, with the frustrated captain questioning the manager's tactics after the Como defeat.

Carrick claimed it was a "pure football" decision before the match rather than punishment but decided against giving him a minute.

Fernandes was also at Carrington on Monday -- a day off for the players -- to receive what is understood to be pre-planned treatment.

The skipper's eye-catching remarks in Italy came a week after Lisandro Martínez was fined and brought in for talks after criticising the club hierarchy in a set of stunning interviews after the loss at Atlético Madrid.

stories.headline: MLB tests out restricted OF shifts in effort to up offense
stories.summary: Major League Baseball, in an effort to boost offense, is testing out limited outfield shifts during this year's Arizona Fall League, as players consult a videoboard to see if they are properly positioned.
stories.body:
SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. -- The Arizona Fall League has long been a testing ground for the next generation of MLB players, and lately, it's also been a venue for testing potential rules changes.

This year, Major League Baseball's newest experiment is to restrict the positioning of outfielders on every at-bat.

The goal is to boost the game's sluggish offense by making outfielders play straight up -- instead of adjusting for individual hitters' tendencies -- which will in theory lead to more doubles and triples.

The outfield positioning experiment is limited to just games that are played at Salt River Fields, since it has similar technology to MLB parks.

How it works is outfielders will look up at a small video board that can tell a player where they are in the field and will either generate an "X," if he's incorrectly positioned or an "O" if he is in a defensively acceptable spot.

Minnesota Twins prospect Kyle DeBarge is getting experience with the experimental system.

"The hardest part is cutting off doubles in the gap and they're even turning into triples," DeBarge said. "That's what they told us they wanted in the beginning. So it works."

The experimental rules force outfielders at Salt River Fields to play much more shallow than they would in most situations, which means they are forced to go back on fly balls much more often than normal. The flip side is that there are almost no bloop singles.

A recent game saw Scottsdale beat Salt River 15-8 in a tilt that featured five triples -- which was an AFL record.

"We talked to our guys about embracing it, it only happens in our ballpark, so embrace it and move on," Salt River manager Ted Tom said. "There's going to be some things that we've never seen before. That's OK, just keep playing."

The league has spent years attempting to increase both the speed of games and offense, with mixed results.

The pitch clock was the biggest change -- and drastically reduced game times -- but there were also tweaks that included rules on infield shifts, bigger bases and a limit on how many times a pitcher could disengage from the rubber.

Game times are about 25 minutes shorter and stolen bases are up, but batting average (.243 in 2022 and .244 in 2026), runs per game (4.28 in 2022, 4.48 in 2026) and hits per game (8.16 in 2022, 8.20 in 2026) haven't changed much.

MLB feels that the AFL is a good opportunity to test rules in a relatively low-stakes environment. The league declined official comment on the most recent experiment, and any change to big-league rules would still be years away.

"The pros are that you're never out of the game, it's very exciting for the fans and there's lots of action, which is part of the intention," Tom said.

But when asked if he thought these new outfield defensive positioning rules were straying a bit too far, Tom gave a little grin before mimicking a zipper across his lips.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.summary: The NBA is back. The buzz never left. Bookmark this page for the latest news, rumblings and analysis from ESPN's insiders.
stories.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops.

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season long, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Windhorst on what the Jalen Williams injury means in OKC: "I guess I should put my Bobby Marks hat on just because what you want in a podcast is you want analysis of this beyond just a visceral response. The Thunder have the ability to apply for a disabled player exception. But let's be honest here, they cannot replace him."

"They'll replace him with what they have on their roster with Ajay Mitchell. He becomes a very important piece right now and the fact that they had to trade away multiple wings over the summer -- Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort ... It comes into play for sure, but this means Ajay Mitchell will have to have a big season and now Cason Wallace, who was just rewarded with a huge contract, those guys will be needed. And you also could see some opportunities for Bennett Stirtz, who actually I think got his first NBA basket tonight. So there's probably no team that could withstand an injury like this other than the Thunder.

"They can apply for a disabled player exception, which they will certainly get. They will get, I believe, the full mid-level exception that they can use up to the mid-level exception, which is like, $14-ish million that they can use to to sign a player or trade for a player. They can only trade for a player with that exception who's got one year left on his contract.

"They're a very expensive roster. That's one of the reasons why they made those trades. So I cannot see them leaning into that. They're already deep and they're very expensive. So I think it's unlikely they take advantage of that, but there is a mechanism that exists."

Windhorst on the Gary Trent Jr. situation in Milwaukee: "I will tell you that it is a frequent conversation as I talk with people around the league. You know, they're like, 'Do you hear anything on the Gary Trent investigation? Do you hear anything on the Gary Trent investigation?' It is being done by a different law firm than did the Clippers investigation. They were sort of twin investigations.

"I will just say I was talking to an executive the other day and he just said if this was a pre-existing deal and let's just be honest, the word of this deal was out there in the spring. I had an executive say to me that they think, and I want to be clear, I want to be cautious, but I had an executive say to me, if this is proven to be true, then this is actually more egregious than the Clippers deal. When you think of it, the Clippers didn't get any salary cap relief for their salary cap circumvention. They were just funneling their max player more money.

In the case of the Bucks, allegedly Gary Trent signed back-to-back minimum contracts and then got this $64 million deal. "Well, I'm just saying if you're going to compare it to Joe Smith ... this is more comparable to what happened with Joe Smith if indeed they are found guilty."

Slater on a Porzingis' status in Golden State: "He was around the team in the week leading up to training camp. He went to this event with Jimmy Butler in San Diego, but if you talk to players and people at that event, he wasn't getting on the court. He wasn't in the weight room. He would show up to more of the dinners and the fun stuff.

"But it seemed clear right before camp that he was fading away from basketball, obviously dealing with this health issue and thinking about his future. He calls Mike Dunleavy the day before training camp, basically tells him he's not coming in to work, he's going to go deal with this health thing.

"He showed up for one meeting two weeks into camp as the Warriors team was in Las Vegas. He met with Mike Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini. From my understanding, those are pretty much the only two he's been communicating with during this entire process. After that meeting, the Warriors announced that he was going to be around the team. Then he left the facility and hasn't returned and has not been around the team to the point that when we put out the report yesterday, the Warriors didn't address some of the trade speculation, but did say he will not be around the team in the immediate future.

"Clearly, this is something, as you mentioned, that Mike Dunleavy's called around the league and explored."

Marks: Warriors have hurdles in a potential Porzingis deal
Following the news that the Warriors are exploring deals, finding a trade early in the season for Kristaps Porzingis could be difficult.

First, Golden State is hard capped at the second apron and isn't allowed to take back more salary than what is sent out. The Warriors are allowed to aggregate salaries if they are receiving less money in return.

Second, since teams are in the evaluation periods of their rosters, trades are uncommon early in the season.

Under the current CBA, there have only been two regular season trades in the months of October and November. -- Bobby Marks

Ishbia on the future of NBA expansion: "Well, I'm supportive of growing the game. So I'm pro expansion.

"Obviously, it depends on the situation and making sure that it's the right partners because they're now partners with us. And the right value, but also are they doing the right things for the fans? I believe that Vegas is a market that we need to fill. I think Seattle's one. I know there's been talk about Mexico City. The way I look at it is expanding the game. The NBA is a global game. And so having 30 is a limited number. Can you get to 32? I mean, can you go that many more? So, it's like, can you grow? Can you cover a big market like Vegas?

"I don't care that it's close to Phoenix. I'm excited. I think there's abundance. There's opportunity everywhere. And I'm supportive of it."

Ishbia on the outlook of the 2026-27 NBA season: "First off, there's a lot more balance. The East definitely got stronger. The West is extremely strong. But let's put it aside.

"There's also no tanking. So there's not five free wins, eight free wins. And in the East last year, a lot of teams really compounded that because there was about seven teams, six teams trying to lose, which is horrible for our game. NBA Adam Silver did a great job. We got rid of that. So there's no tanking.

"People are going to win -- 45 wins is a hell of a season. And I think it's going to be very, very tough. And I think that might be a 4, 5, 6 seed where last year it was 50, 52 wins to get to that level. And so, I think that's not been talked about enough."

Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected
The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row.

"We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling
Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title:

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Fernando Alonso lashes out at 'quality of drivers' at bottom of F1 grid
stories.summary: Fernando Alonso has hit out at Alex Albon after a collision on the opening lap of the United States Grand Prix, saying the quality of drivers in the bottom third of the grid "is very low."
stories.body:
Fernando Alonso has hit out at Alex Albon after a collision on the opening lap of the United States Grand Prix, saying the quality of drivers in the bottom third of the grid "is very low."

The pair clashed after the Williams driver tried to pass Alonso at the Turn 11 hairpin at the Circuit of the Americas for 12th place.

The stewards decided not to hand out penalties, but it ultimately cost Alonso four places and left his Aston Martin with floor damage. He finished the race down in 16th, with no points on the board.

"Albon forgot that corner 11 was there and he had to turn left," Alonso said.

"I think when you start at the back there is this risk always. I think the quality of the drivers in the lower third of the grid is very low, as we saw today with Alex.

"So I think we need to improve the car and start a little bit higher up."

- Kimi Antonelli wins United States GP but made to wait for first F1 title

- Toto Wolff hails Kimi Antonelli on U.S GP win: 'The race of a champion who isn't a champion yet'

- George Russell: Finishing second in F1 title race 'doesn't mean anything'

Alonso felt that the damage to his car was causing him to lose half a second or more per lap and that he finished the race with "half a car."

"That was the biggest damage," he said. "I think we lost half a second or more [per lap]. The car is destroyed; I saw it in parc ferme. Half of the floor is not there. I don't know how we kept on going and how we were semi-competitive.

"I imagine if the car was in one piece, probably today the points were a strong possibility because we were running P12 with half a car."

Albon, who finished in 17th, believed he gave Alonso enough "space" but that he also got damage and was running with a broken wing.

"It felt like there was a car on the right side of Fernando," Albon said. "And he gave Fernando enough space as if he thought there was only one car on his inside. But then I was on the inside of Fernando.

"So then I think it pinched and I tried to get out of the way and get on the kerb. But I didn't make good of it. So I imagine he got damage. I know I got damaged as we were driving around with a broken wing for the race."

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Revs jump eight places as playoffs loom
stories.summary: We're getting down to the pointy end of the season, and the New England Revolution have jumped right up ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

Nashville officially claimed the 2026 Supporters' Shield on Saturday with a 2-0 win over Montreal. Just five points away from the single-season points record with three matches to go, more history is in sight for the best team in MLS.

2. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 2

Without Lionel Messi in the starting lineup, Miami looked lost in their 2-0 defeat to Red Bull New York. Despite dominating possession, they created little and left an open runway for their hosts to attack in the other direction. This Miami outfit is still wildly streaky.

3. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 3

Following their midweek U.S. Open Cup triumph, St. Louis understandably rotated their lineup for Saturday's clash against Salt Lake. Tomas Ostrak getting himself sent off in the first half hampered the visitor's chances of claiming a result in Utah, and a 3-0 defeat followed.

4. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 12

Up to second in the East after a 2-1 triumph over Philadelphia, that the Revolution continue to thrive in the absence of key starters Jack Harrison and Alhassan Yusuf is nothing short of impressive. Against the Union, Matt Turner's standout showing helped them collect all three points.

5. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 6

Chicago got off to a slow start in Atlanta, conceding inside of five minutes, but managing to score three unanswered en route to a 3-2 victory. However, it is a concern that Robert Lewandowski has gone scoreless in six straight starts.

6. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 4

The Union's unbeaten streak -- one that stretched all the way back to July -- was snapped after a 2-1 loss to New England. Missing Cavan Sullivan in the attack due to injury made life difficult for Philadelphia, as did a late penalty concession from teenage center back Neil Pierre.

7. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 5

Vancouver didn't look like themselves in a 1-0 loss to Colorado, creating little in the first half before an only slightly more energetic second period. Thomas Müller's injury, mixed with Sebastian Berhalter's summer exit, seems to have forced the Whitecaps down a rung in the chance creation department.

8. LAFC
Previous ranking: 8

It wasn't pretty, but LAFC came back from a two-goal deficit to earn a 2-2 draw with the Galaxy. There seemed to be a lack of tactical clarity from the team's attacking players, which isn't a surprise given interim manager Xavi Tamarit has only recently begun his tenure. Still, there's much polishing to be done with the playoffs right around the corner.

9. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 13

Rarely a team to control games with short passes, Dallas averaged more than 50% possession for only the second time all season in their 3-0 victory over San Jose. Forced to keep the ball for stretches by a defiant Earthquakes outfit, the hosts made the best of it.

10. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 10

The Sounders had a road win against San Diego nearly wrapped up, but a late penalty converted by Cédric Bakambu forced a draw. Though Saturday's finish was frustrating, it's a positive for the Sounders that they've lost just one of their last 12 games.

11. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 9

A late, 100th-minute concession turned three points into one for Orlando, as their matchup with New York City finished in a 2-2 draw. Still, the Lions have gone four unbeaten and Martín Ojeda and Antoine Griezmann continued to shine. Both claimed a goal on Saturday.

12. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 17

They had the benefit of playing Miami without Messi in the starting lineup, yes. But Red Bull New York looked dominant against their still-talented Eastern Conference foes in a 2-0 home win. With young midfielders Adri Mehmeti and Ronald Donkor showing out, the Red Bulls may yet hold onto the final wildcard spot out East.

13. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 7

It's unlike Dean Smith's Charlotte team to be carved open with ease, but that's exactly what happened on the road in Portland. In a 3-2 loss, Charlotte allowed 27 shots, 20 of which came from inside their own box. The sooner Smith's side can forget Saturday, the better.

14. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 20

Already used in a host of roles since he arrived from Middlesbrough in the summer, Morgan Whittaker scored the lone goal in Colorado's 1-0 victory over Vancouver. The Englishman started up top, finished on the wing, and has even played in midfield. His varied employment helps make the Rapids hard to pin down.

15. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 15

Without Niko Tsakiris in the starting lineup, San Jose simply isn't a major threat. The star playmaker managed a late substitute appearance on his way back from injury in the Earthquakes' 3-0 loss to Dallas, but it wasn't enough to save the side from a poor result.

16. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 11

Acutely missing Jack McGlynn following his summer exit, the Dynamo created very little in a 0-0 draw with Minnesota. Once a team that looked poised to claim a home playoff spot in the West, Houston have now fallen out of the top four.

17. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 14

Evander is an undoubtedly polarizing figure in Cincinnati, but the Brazilian attacking midfielder scored a wonder-goal and collected a lovely assist in his team's 2-0 road win over D.C. United. On his day, few players in MLS are more likely to brute-force a victory than Evander.

18. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 23

Helped by a first-half sending off that reduced St. Louis to just 10 men, Salt Lake put together a dominant 3-0 victory to keep their playoff hopes alive. Even before their opponents saw their numbers decreased, RSL looked something like their early season selves. Currently 10th in the West, hope is still alive.

19. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 18

Despite holding a 2-0 lead over bitter rivals LAFC in Sunday's lone MLS fixture, the Galaxy folded in the second half to end the evening with a 2-2 draw. Surrounded in the table by fellow playoff hopefuls who have a game in hand, questions abound in Carson.

20. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 21

Though the disappointment of falling in the midweek U.S. Open Cup final remains, Columbus bounced back with a 4-2 victory over Toronto. Currently just one spot below the East's playoff line, a postseason berth may yet await the Crew after a brutal start to the year.

21. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 16

New York City's playoff hopes are hanging by a thread, so that Jonny Shore managed a 100th minute equalizer to rescue a 2-2 draw in Orlando was crucial. Still, things aren't going right for NYCFC: big-money summer signing Bénie Traoré has started just two of the club's last seven games.

22. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 25

The Timbers topped Charlotte by a 3-2 scoreline, helped by homegrown signing Eric Izoita's pair of assists. The 19-year-old signed a first team contract last month and is already a key part of manager Marti Cifuentes' plans.

23. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 19

Far too often in 2026, Minnesota's attack has looked listless. That was the case in a 0-0 draw with Houston, one made even more difficult for the Loons due to Joaquin Pereyra's continued absence from the starting lineup as he recovers from a quad injury.

24. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 26

Though they conceded chances along the way, Austin earned a 2-1 victory over Kansas City thanks to a brace from Myrto Uzuni. Even with bright young midfielder Ervin Torres' first-half injury exit, the Texan side is still building nicely towards 2027.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 22

Toronto couldn't have had a worse start to a must-win game in their 4-2 defeat at the hands of the Crew, conceding four straight goals before answering back. The road to the playoffs for Robin Fraser's team got far bumpier this weekend.

26. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 24

San Diego drew 2-2 with Seattle, extending their streak of games where they've allowed at least two goals to eight in a row. The sophomore side can't keep the ball out of their own net and their postseason hopes look dim as a result.

27. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 27

D.C. managed only three shots inside Cincinnati's box in a 2-0 home defeat on Saturday. They simply lacked the firepower to go toe-to-toe with Cincinnati and now look destined to miss the postseason.

28. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

Now one goal shy of tying MLS's all-time record for goals conceded in a single season (one set by San Jose in 2024 with 78 allowed), Kansas City fell 2-1 to Austin. Sloppy box defending dashed any chance the home side had of earning a result.

29. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

Outside of Breel Embolo's performance, there was precious little for Atlanta to write home about in their 3-2 loss to Chicago. This team needs a hard offseason reset.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Just days after losing the Canadian Championship in embarrassing fashion to Forge FC, Montréal fell 2-0 to Nashville. Officially eliminated from playoff contention, it was another bleak year for Montréal.

stories.headline: Alexander Volkanovski could face a new challenge after UFC 333
stories.summary: Alexander Volkanovski and Petr Yan defended titles at UFC 333, but which champion could fight in a new division?
stories.body:
While both champions who topped the UFC 333 fight card successfully defended their belts, their next moves will likely be in different directions.

Featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski needed only two rounds to put away formerly unbeaten challenger Movsar Evloev. Now, he could try his luck again in the weight class that is home to two of his three UFC losses.

Meanwhile, men's bantamweight champion Petr Yan beat Merab Dvalishvili by unanimous decision to close his trilogy with the former titleholder. Yan could follow his trilogy bout with another rematch, as two possible challengers have already faced him in the Octagon -- including one who already holds a victory over Yan.

Let's take a look at the most likely scenarios and a wild card for Volkanovski, Yan and more winners and losers on the UFC 333 main card.

Alexander Volkanovski, featherweight champion
Who should be next: Charles Oliveira

If Oliveira successfully defends the BMF title against Diego Lopes at UFC 335 in December, this is the fight to make. Both are MMA legends, and neither has shown signs of falling off. Making this fight in 2027 wouldn't feel like an attempt to squeeze name value out of two fading fighters. It would feel as if it was happening right at the right time. The BMF angle doesn't add much for me, but if the UFC is going to keep that belt going, Volkanovski is more than qualified to fight for it. It would also give Volkanovski a chance to prove himself as a lightweight title contender. He told ESPN in September he didn't love the idea of jumping the line at lightweight to fight Justin Gaethje, especially with an obvious title challenger like Arman Tsarukyan. The BMF fight would legitimize the winner as a real challenger for the 155-pound belt.

Wild card: Tsarukyan

Gaethje hasn't said whether he intends to fight again. If he does, Tsarukyan is next. Gaethje has said he's next in line, and the UFC has told Tsarukyan he is. But if Gaethje decides to walk into the sunset after that White House win in June, there'd obviously be a vacant slot. Volkanovski deserves it. Send him straight into the title shot against Tsarukyan.

Movsar Evloev, featherweight
Who should be next: Pat Sabatini

I didn't love Evloev's choice of words, of "maybe I'll try again," regarding his future as a featherweight title challenger. Perhaps chalk that up to English being his second language. Hopefully, he won't be too discouraged by his first loss coming at the hands of the greatest 145-pounder ever. Regardless of his mindset, he is undeniably in a tough spot. It took him a long time to get to the top. It's probably a safe bet it will take him a while to get back. He will be in the position of gatekeeper for a minute. There's no other way to say it. The most obvious name in that group right now is Sabatini, who is 9-2 in the UFC.

Wild card: Steve Garcia

Garcia would be the second-most obvious name in that category, coming off a loss to Diego Lopes at UFC Freedom 250 in June.

Petr Yan, men's bantamweight champion

Who should be next: Sean O'Malley

Yan vs. O'Malley is the biggest fight available. Has O'Malley really earned a title shot? Since losing to Merab Dvalishvili in 2024 and 2025, he's only 2-0 -- with a close win over Song Yadong and a knockout of Aiemann Zahabi. Those two wins don't scream title shot, to be fair. But it's also impossible to strongly argue against O'Malley. He holds a victory (albeit a controversial one) over Yan from 2022. Beyond O'Malley, Song has the strongest case for a title shot -- and O'Malley just beat him in January. Even if you thought O'Malley lost to Yan back in 2022, it was a fantastic, competitive fight. We always knew the UFC would revisit it someday. I don't see why that day wouldn't be now.

Wild card: Song

If the UFC wants to give Yan this rematch instead, I'm in favor. It makes the most sense to go with O'Malley, but as a fight fan, I like the idea of Yan vs. Song, probably because of how Song knocked out Umar Nurmagomedov with one shot in the pocket. Yan vs. O'Malley would be an interesting chess match, but Song's firepower and speed are game changers. Yan will likely face both fighters eventually. O'Malley makes more sense to come first for a variety of reasons, but the more explosive matchup for Yan might be Song.

Merab Dvalishvili, men's bantamweight
Who should be next: Umar Nurmagomedov

I wouldn't expect Dvalishvili to sit on the sideline very long. He was just forced to wait 10 months for his trilogy bout with Yan, and now he's coming off the disappointment of his second loss in a row. I imagine he'll be eager to get back in the cage. The Nurmagomedov rematch is honestly a no-brainer. There's genuine heat between them. Nurmagomedov will presumably want to return by January, before he observes the Muslim holiday of Ramadan beginning in February. Their first fight was fight of the night at UFC 311 in January 2025. Nurmagomedov broke his hand early in that bout, and Dvalishvili later revealed he fought through injuries during camp. Now, both are coming off a loss, which the UFC loves to consider in matchmaking. There's a million reasons to run this one back, and I expect the UFC to do it.

Wild card: Payton Talbott

This makes sense for obvious reasons. It's a big jump in competition for Talbott, but he has earned the right to make it. Talbott has shown the kind of potential the UFC can -- and will -- reward with shortcuts. He doesn't need to beat Nos. 5 through 10 in the divisional rankings to earn a title shot. It still feels early for Talbott to make this sort of leap, but it's also the right moment to face a former champion. If Talbott loses, it's no big deal, because, at 28 years old, he still has plenty of time. If he wins, he becomes a legitimate title contender overnight.

Aaron Pico, featherweight

Who should be next: Jean Silva

I suggested this matchup after Pico's last win over Patricio Pitbull in April, and I see no reason not to double down. On paper, it's arguably the most explosive fight in the division -- especially with Diego Lopes moving to lightweight to fight Charles Oliveira in December. Silva would be a big jump up the rankings for Pico, but honestly, it's a bigger fight for Silva than most other potential top-10 matchups. Pico has always shown unmatched potential, but has fallen victim to devastating finishes throughout his career. This potential UFC Fight Night main event would be one of the scariest fights in the division for Pico. Let's see how he handles it.

Wild card: Youssef Zalal

Zalal, 30, has had an interesting career. He signed with the UFC in 2020 with a lot of hype, then went 0-3 and was cut in 2021. He fought his way back to the promotion and won five in a row before losing to Aljamain Sterling in April. A matchup against Pico would pit two featherweights against each other who have shown immense potential but haven't fully realized it.
